paragraphs: Before opening, baristas calibrate machines and prepare beans and milk. During the morning rush, they produce drinks continuously while monitoring extraction and milk texture. At midday, they discuss beans and brewing with guests and make signature drinks. The afternoon brings restocking and equipment cleaning, followed by inventory and a full bar cleanup before closing.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 3,796,000 baristas were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 4,029,200 by 2034, a net increase of about 233,200 jobs, with approximately 904,300 openings each year. Median annual pay is about $30,500 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace baristas, but it will reduce standardized roles. Automated coffee machines and convenience-store service accelerate basic Americanos and lattes, shifting baristas from standard drinks toward specialty pour-overs, signature beverage development, guest relationships, and experience. People limited to basic drinks face the most pressure, while baristas with flavor knowledge and hospitality skills become more valuable.
